content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Boston

steps_items.heading: 1. Verify Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a combination of formal education and documented project-management experience. Review PMI's specific hour and credential thresholds for your background. Granite PM Academy's admissions team can confirm whether you meet requirements before enrollment.

steps_items.heading: 2. Complete 35 Contact Hours Online
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP Bootcamp. Attend synchronous sessions on your schedule—no commute, no fixed classroom location. Our active certified practitioners deliver the full PMI curriculum required for exam eligibility.

steps_items.heading: 3. Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After completing the bootcamp, submit your PMP application directly to PMI, including proof of your 35 contact hours and project experience. Pay PMI's exam fee to secure your test date and official candidate status.

steps_items.heading: 4. Prepare and Test
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice exams, study guides, and instructor Q&A support—to solidify your knowledge. Schedule your proctored exam at a Pearson VUE testing center and sit for the PMP assessment.

steps_items.heading: 5. Maintain Your Credential
steps_items.text: After passing, you'll hold the PMP for a three-year cycle. Earn professional development units (PDUs) through continuing education, work experience, and community involvement to renew. Granite PM Academy offers PDU-eligible courses to support your ongoing maintenance.
